name: Citrix HDX / ICA
description: The oldest of the big three enterprise VDI protocols (ICA dates back to the early 1990s, long before RDP existed), now branded HDX within Citrix Virtual Apps and Desktops. Its Thinwire technology selectively applies H.264/H.265/AV1 only to moving regions of the screen while keeping text and static content losslessly compressed.

Wayland Unattended Access.comment: Tech-preview support (VDA 2603) on RHEL/Rocky/Ubuntu, but HDX 3D Pro and Linux app sessions aren't supported under it yet

Multi-Monitor Support.comment: Plug-and-play multi-monitor, with up to ~4K per window

Microphone Passthrough.comment: HDX RealTime supports bidirectional audio for webcam/softphone scenarios

Adaptive Bitrate.comment: Thinwire adaptive display selectively encodes only actively-changing screen regions

H.265 Codec.comment: Including 4:4:4 support since Citrix Workspace app 2305, with GPU-offloaded decoding

AV1 Codec.comment: Supported on both NVIDIA and Intel GPUs

Multi-User Sessions.comment: One of Citrix's original strengths — shared-session hosting (formerly XenApp) for many concurrent users per server

4:4:4 Chroma Subsampling.comment: "Visually lossless" YUV 4:4:4 mode is supported, plus a true "Pixel perfect" fully lossless option

Frame Rate (FPS).comment: No fixed number; H.265 4:4:4 support alone was measured internally at ~4x the FPS of H.264 4:4:4 at the same bandwidth

Session Recording.comment: Citrix Session Recording is a named feature within Citrix Virtual Apps and Desktops

ISO Mounting.comment: Client drive mapping exists, but that's not literal virtual-media/ISO mounting

Wake-on-LAN.comment: Supported for Remote PC Access scenarios (waking physical office PCs)

Pre-Login Access.comment: Users authenticate via Citrix Workspace/StoreFront first, then reach the delivered session

Shared Clipboard.comment: Bidirectional, with policy-level controls for security

2FA / MFA.comment: Supported via NetScaler Gateway/Citrix Workspace identity integration, not a core ICA protocol feature itself

Windows: Host.comment: The primary VDA (Virtual Delivery Agent) platform

macOS: Host.comment: Citrix doesn't deliver virtualized macOS desktops

Linux X11: Host.comment: Actively developed Linux VDA, e.g. version 2603

Linux Wayland: Host.comment: Tech-preview status with notable limitations (no HDX 3D Pro, no app-only sessions)

Linux: Client.comment: Actively maintained, recently gained general-availability ARM64 support

NVIDIA RTX 4090.comment: Targets datacenter/professional GPUs (NVIDIA GRID, Intel Iris Pro) for hardware encoding, not consumer GeForce cards

Intel iGPU (QuickSync).comment: Intel Iris Pro hardware encoding is explicitly supported, but no consumer-benchmark table is published

Personal: Monthly.comment: Enterprise VDI product, not sold to individuals

Team / Business: Monthly.comment: Sold as per-user/per-device subscriptions to Citrix Virtual Apps and Desktops, not a self-serve price

Enterprise.comment: Quoted through Citrix/reseller channels based on user count and edition
